clue.text: Impasse when Don is in trouble among the workforce

indicators.note: the scrambled name is placed among the letters of the staff word, i.e. inside it

parts.note: the workforce of a company is its staff

indicators.note: a name in trouble is in disorder, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A workplace standoff arises when a man called Don gets into trouble with his colleagues.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are words for a deadlock in which neither side will give way.

clue.text: Film actor showing vigour after short time

indicators.note: the vigorous word comes after the abbreviation, so the time letter goes first

parts.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
racy writing or performance is lively and full of vigour

explanation.surface: A screen actor shows energy after a brief period.
explanation.walkthrough: Spencer Tracy was a Hollywood star of the 1930s to 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: Spencer Tracy is an example of a film actor, a two-time Oscar winner.

clue.text: Donne in translation — writing becomes dull?

indicators.note: a text in translation is carried into another form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: script is a style of handwriting or a written text

explanation.surface: Translating the poet John Donne may leave his lively writing flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in translation' turns DONNE into NONDE, followed by SCRIPT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lacking distinctive character is described as featureless or dull.

clue.text: I sit with toes twisted — that produces a sort of pain

indicators.note: toes that are twisted are bent out of shape, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Sitting with one's toes twisted under is bound to hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted' rearranges ISIT plus TOES. The definition is loose: the condition is a bone inflammation, which causes pain.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an inflammation of bone, a painful medical condition, loosely called a kind of pain.

clue.text: Pioneers who could be hot and suffering

indicators.note: the fodder words could be something else once their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Early settlers who might have been feeling the heat and enduring hardship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges all fifteen letters of HOT AND SUFFERING.
explanation.definitionFit: The founders of a nation or movement were its originators, its pioneers.

clue.text: Test applied to personal form of music

parts.note: the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for vehicles in Britain
something personal is one's own

explanation.surface: An examination applied to one's own kind of music.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is Britain's yearly compulsory vehicle safety check.
explanation.definitionFit: The Detroit record label gave its name to a soul and pop style, a genre of music.

clue.text: Maureen, attractive girl in the latest fashion?

parts.note: Mo is a common short form of the name Maureen
a dish is slang for an attractive person

explanation.surface: Maureen is a pretty girl dressed in the newest style.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stylish and up to date means following the current trend.

clue.text: Feature of Dartmoor almost rent apart

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: rent apart means torn

explanation.surface: Something on Dartmoor has nearly been ripped to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: Dartmoor is a moorland area in Devon, England, famous for its rocky hilltops.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocky hilltop outcrop is the classic landscape feature of Dartmoor.

clue.text: Put on paper the fall in value of an asset

definitions.text: the fall in value of an asset
definitions.meaning: an accounting term for reducing an asset's book value

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to record in writing; as a noun it is an accounting reduction in an asset's book value.

clue.text: Periodical to take home, something attractive

parts.note: mag is short for magazine, a periodical
to net a sum is to take it home as pay after deductions

explanation.surface: A magazine to bring home that has real appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: It attracts iron, and figuratively anything that draws people in.

clue.text: Support wicked nun full of false pride

indicators.note: the scrambled nun is filled with the other scrambled word, so it goes inside
a wicked nun is twisted from her proper form, so her letters are jumbled
false pride is not genuine, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wicked nun bursting with vanity hardly offers support.
explanation.definitionFit: To prop up or provide a foundation for something is to support it.

clue.text: Barn close to river, middle of field

parts.note: by means near or close to

indicators.note: the central letter of the five-letter word is taken

explanation.surface: A barn stands near a river in the centre of a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' picks the E from the centre of field.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a cowshed, a farm building of the barn type.

clue.text: I'd spend, so I could become unwell

indicators.note: the fodder could become another word once its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone frets that spending too much might make them ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Being slightly ill or out of sorts is a formal synonym for unwell.

clue.text: Drink with harmony after work — good time

indicators.note: the drink and harmony words come after the work abbreviation

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
port is a fortified wine
unity is agreement or harmony

explanation.surface: A drink in friendly company after work makes for a good time.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition means a well-timed chance, not a pleasant evening out.
explanation.definitionFit: A favourable moment for doing something is a chance, a good time to act.

clue.text: Bringing out attraction that gets son led astray

indicators.note: the son is led away and lost from the word, so his letter is removed

parts.note: seduction is the act of attracting or enticing
S is the abbreviation for son, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: An allure that leads a son into wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'led astray' takes S from SEDUCTION, playing on seduction leading people astray.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a technical word for drawing out or extracting, from the Latin for leading out.

clue.text: Doctor with a trick, man proving to be very cruel

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle
Ian is a man's name

explanation.surface: A doctor and a swindler turn out to be a heartless man.
explanation.definitionFit: Harsh and severe laws are named after Draco, the strict lawgiver of ancient Athens.

clue.text: Low-quality gold found by river

parts.note: the Po is the longest river in Italy
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Inferior gold has been found beside a river, as a prospector might grumble.
explanation.walkthrough: Gold is written before the river but goes second, since 'found by' only says the two sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of inferior standard is said to be bad or shoddy.

clue.text: Transfer from hospital somewhere in Hampshire

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
Andover is a town in Hampshire

explanation.surface: A patient is moved from a hospital somewhere in Hampshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampshire is a county in southern England; Andover is one of its towns.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing control or responsibility from one party to another is a transfer.

clue.text: Graduate and soldier, men on special quest

parts.note: an MA is a Master of Arts graduate
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A graduate and a soldier set out on an important mission.
explanation.definitionFit: The wise men followed the star to Bethlehem, a mission to find the infant Jesus.

clue.text: Notorious harangue with signal first

indicators.note: the signal word is placed first, ahead of the harangue word

parts.note: a flag is used to signal
a rant is a harangue, a long angry speech

explanation.surface: A tirade, prompted by a signal, that is shocking.
explanation.definitionFit: Conspicuously bad conduct is glaring, blatant or notorious.

clue.text: Unacceptable person rendering song in public house

indicators.note: the song is placed in the abbreviation for the pub

parts.note: PH is the abbreviation for public house on maps
an aria is a solo song in opera

explanation.surface: Someone singing in a pub makes themselves unwelcome.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcast, someone shunned by society, is an unacceptable person.

clue.text: Given an agreement that's shortened

definitions.meaning: engaged under a formal deal or contract

explanation.surface: A deal has been signed, but the terms have been cut back.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is engaged under a formal deal; the other is reduced in size or length.

clue.text: Note by you and me provides reasons for choosing product

parts.note: us is you and me together
a PS is a postscript, a note added to a letter

explanation.surface: A note from the two of us lists why to buy an item.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters are an abbreviation for unique selling points, a marketing term.
explanation.definitionFit: Unique selling points are the features that make a buyer choose one product over another.

clue.text: Groom is quiet and naive, not good

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical direction for quiet

indicators.note: not signals that the good letter is removed

parts.note: green means inexperienced or naive

explanation.surface: A bridegroom who is shy and innocent, but not a good one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes G from GREEN. 'Groom' here is the verb, not the bridegroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to tidy and smarten one's appearance, as a bird does its feathers.

clue.text: Criticise blokes heard in act of deception

parts.note: to dis is slang for to criticise or disrespect

indicators.note: heard signals that the bloke word is said aloud, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: guys are blokes, men

explanation.surface: Speaking ill of men caught out in a trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Hiding one's identity, a pretence or false appearance, is a deception.

clue.text: Animal eating nuts, but not the whole lot

indicators.note: only part of the two words is used, the letters sitting inside them

explanation.surface: An animal munching nuts but leaving some uneaten.
explanation.definitionFit: The wildebeest is an African antelope, an animal much loved by setters.

clue.text: They may be audible acts of wickedness, nothing being concealed

indicators.note: the zero is hidden away inside the word for sins

parts.note: vices are wicked habits or acts
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Wicked deeds might be overheard, with nothing kept secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking sounds can be heard, so they are things that may be audible.

clue.text: The makings of a feast? Say no more!

definitions.meaning: from the proverb that a sufficiency is as good as a feast
an exclamation telling someone to stop

explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says a sufficiency is as good as a feast, and the word alone is an exclamation meaning stop.

clue.text: Errant man caught in police operation

indicators.note: the man is caught inside the police operation word

parts.note: a sting is an undercover operation by police
Ray is a man's name

explanation.surface: A wayward man is caught in a police trap.
explanation.definitionFit: Errant means wandering off course, which is going astray.
